nodes.name: allowedQuote
nodes.signature: function allowedQuote(address quote) external view returns (bool)
nodes.authority: anyone (declaration only, no body in this file; the selector is dispatched by propose through a low-level staticcall on the owner-set registry address)
nodes.reachability: Declaration only: `allowedQuote` (CauldronGovernor.sol:25) has no body here. Its selector is encoded by `abi.encodeWithSelector` (CauldronGovernor.sol:340) and dispatched by `staticcall` (CauldronGovernor.sol:339) inside propose, where a failed call, a short return or a false decode all revert `QuoteNotAllowed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:342). The callee address is the storage slot `registry` (CauldronGovernor.sol:339), so the code actually reached is the registry's public allowlist mapping `allowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:321), which is written only by the owner-gated `setAllowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:308) and pre-seeded true for native ether at `allowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:175).

nodes.name: renounceOwnership
nodes.signature: function renounceOwnership() public view override onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Override that disables OpenZeppelin's live `renounceOwnership` by reverting `OwnershipCannotBeRenounced` (CauldronGovernor.sol:196). The owner is the only caller of `setRegistry` (CauldronGovernor.sol:251), so renouncing would permanently pin the registry wiring with no redeploy that preserves the stockpiled mandates. `transferOwnership` is untouched, so handing the seat away remains available (DERIVED).
nodes.authority_gate_quote: function renounceOwnership() public view override onlyOwner { (CauldronGovernor.sol:195)

nodes.signature: constructor(address _mifrens) Ownable(msg.sender)
nodes.reachability: Runs once at deployment. A zero electorate reverts `EmptyField` (CauldronGovernor.sol:244); otherwise the voting token is frozen into the immutable `mifrens` (CauldronGovernor.sol:245) that every later weight read uses. `Ownable` (CauldronGovernor.sol:243) installs the deployer as owner, and the owner is the only account that can ever wire `registry` (CauldronGovernor.sol:254). The registry is NOT set here, so until `setRegistry` (CauldronGovernor.sol:251) runs the only caller `NotRegistry` (CauldronGovernor.sol:476) would accept is address zero, and a non-native quote in propose staticalls address zero, whose empty return fails the length test at `QuoteNotAllowed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:342).

nodes.name: setRegistry
nodes.signature: function setRegistry(address _registry) external onlyOwner
nodes.reachability: Owner-only and one-shot: a non-zero current value reverts `RegistryAlreadySet` (CauldronGovernor.sol:252) and a zero argument reverts `EmptyField` (CauldronGovernor.sol:253), so the consumer address can never be rotated or cleared once written to `registry` (CauldronGovernor.sol:254). Whatever lands here becomes the sole caller accepted by `NotRegistry` (CauldronGovernor.sol:476) and the target of the allowlist `staticcall` (CauldronGovernor.sol:339) in propose. Ownership itself is Ownable's: it can be transferred or renounced, and renouncing before this call leaves `markConsumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:475) permanently unreachable (DERIVED).
observations: comment `markConsumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:20) says the only privileged call is markConsumed, restricted to the registry; code `onlyOwner` (CauldronGovernor.sol:251) adds an owner-gated setter, and `Ownable` (CauldronGovernor.sol:243) adds transferOwnership and renounceOwnership to the external surface.

nodes.name: propose
nodes.signature: function propose( string calldata name, string calldata symbol, MetadataMode mode, string calldata baseURI, address renderer, string calldata website, string calldata socials, uint256 nftSupply, uint256 volumePerNFT, address quote ) external returns (uint256 id)
nodes.authority: voter/holder (any address with non-zero live MiFrens voting power)
nodes.reachability: Permissionless for anyone holding one MiFren of live voting power: `getVotes` (CauldronGovernor.sol:294) must be non-zero, with no deposit, cooldown or per-address cap. Input bounds applied here are empty name/symbol `EmptyField` (CauldronGovernor.sol:295), five byte caps `FieldTooLong` (CauldronGovernor.sol:305), a renderer that must have code `BadRenderer` (CauldronGovernor.sol:310), the collection-size ceiling `SupplyOutOfRange` (CauldronGovernor.sol:316) and, for any non-native quote, the registry allowlist `QuoteNotAllowed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:342). `volumePerNFT` (CauldronGovernor.sol:356) is stored unbounded and reaches the hook through `setNftCurveFrom` (CauldronRegistry.sol:1098). The new id is `proposalCount` (CauldronGovernor.sol:345) incremented, the power snapshot is the current block `snapshot` (CauldronGovernor.sol:359), and the vote closes at `votingEndsAt` (CauldronGovernor.sol:360), i.e. three days out. The record is what `winner` (CauldronGovernor.sol:451) hands the registry and what `relaunch` replays via `winner` (CauldronRegistry.sol:867).
observations: comment `markConsumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:315) says a proposal is untrusted input that must be rejected at this boundary because a deeper revert would freeze the machine; code bounds `nftSupply` (CauldronGovernor.sol:316) and the five strings at `FieldTooLong` (CauldronGovernor.sol:305) but stores `volumePerNFT` (CauldronGovernor.sol:356) unbounded, and it reaches the hook unclamped at `setNftCurveFrom` (CauldronRegistry.sol:1098).

nodes.name: displayName
nodes.signature: function displayName(uint256 proposalId) external view returns (string memory)
nodes.reachability: Unrestricted view. Reverts `UnknownProposal` (CauldronGovernor.sol:371) for an id that was never written, otherwise returns the stored name through the pure library helper `displayName` (CauldronGovernor.sol:372). No state, no value, no reachable side effect.

nodes.name: vote
nodes.signature: function vote(uint256 proposalId) external
nodes.value: none - it only records votes; no asset moves (DERIVED)
nodes.authority: anyone holding checkpointed MiFrens voting power at the proposal's snapshot
nodes.reachability: Permissionless per proposal, once per address: an unknown or already-consumed proposal is refused at `UnknownProposal` (CauldronGovernor.sol:385) and `AlreadyConsumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:386), the window is checked before the double-vote test so a closed vote always reports as closed at `VotingClosed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:391), and repeat voting at `AlreadyVoted` (CauldronGovernor.sol:392). Weight is CHECKPOINTED power at the proposal's snapshot block at `getPastVotes` (CauldronGovernor.sol:398), with the snapshot required to be in the past at `SnapshotNotReady` (CauldronGovernor.sol:397), so moving MiFrens to a fresh wallet mints no new votes. The leader/runner-up hints are still maintained - ties keep the incumbent at `_leaderVotes` (CauldronGovernor.sol:407), and a leader gaining votes is not demoted into its own runner slot at `_leaderId` (CauldronGovernor.sol:410) - and the NEW effect is that every vote also enters the fixed 8-slot bench at `_benchRecord` (CauldronGovernor.sol:421), which is what the leader rescan now walks instead of a positional window over the proposal list.

nodes.name: _benchRecord
nodes.signature: function _benchRecord(uint256 id, uint256 votes) private
observations: eight slots is a hard ceiling on simultaneously-tracked mandates at `BENCH_SLOTS` (CauldronGovernor.sol:200): a ninth live mandate weaker than all eight incumbents is not recorded, so `_recomputeLeader` (CauldronGovernor.sol:554) cannot elect it even though it exists, is settled and is unconsumed (DERIVED)
nodes.reachability: Called on every vote from `_benchRecord` (CauldronGovernor.sol:421). Entry is priced in VOTES rather than position: a proposal already on the bench returns immediately at `b` (CauldronGovernor.sol:434), and otherwise the incoming weight must exceed the WEAKEST live entry at `weakVotes` (CauldronGovernor.sol:443) to displace it. A slot holding a consumed or vanished proposal is valued at zero at `consumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:439) so it is reclaimed first and the bench self-cleans as the machine is reborn. The loop is a fixed `BENCH_SLOTS` (CauldronGovernor.sol:432) = 8 iterations whatever the proposal count, which is what keeps the rebirth scan O(1) (DERIVED). Because displacement needs more votes than the weakest LIVE mandate, a proposal nobody voted for can never enter, and spam filings cost the bench nothing (DERIVED).

nodes.name: winner
nodes.signature: function winner() external view returns (uint256 proposalId, BrewSpec memory spec)
nodes.authority: anyone (the registry is the production caller)
nodes.reachability: Unrestricted view, but only meaningful to the registry: `relaunch` calls `winner` (CauldronRegistry.sol:867) to build the next brew and later retires it with `markConsumed` (CauldronRegistry.sol:995). Selection is delegated to `_bestUnconsumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:452), which returns the cached leader only once its voting window has closed; zero reverts `NoProposals` (CauldronGovernor.sol:453). The returned struct copies seven proposer-controlled strings and addresses into memory, which is the replay cost the byte caps in propose bound.

nodes.name: hasProposals
nodes.signature: function hasProposals() external view returns (bool)
nodes.authority: anyone (the registry is the production caller)
nodes.reachability: Unrestricted view wrapping the same selection as winner. `relaunch` gates the whole rebirth on it at `hasProposals` (CauldronRegistry.sol:805) and reverts `NoProposal` there when it is false, so a false answer stops the machine being reborn until a settled, unconsumed proposal exists. It costs a scan whenever the cached-leader fast path in `_bestUnconsumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:471) misses.

nodes.name: markConsumed
nodes.signature: function markConsumed(uint256 proposalId) external
nodes.reachability: Reachable only from the address stored in `registry` (CauldronGovernor.sol:476), which in production is CauldronRegistry inside relaunch at `markConsumed` (CauldronRegistry.sol:995); any other caller reverts `NotRegistry` (CauldronGovernor.sol:476). It re-checks existence `UnknownProposal` (CauldronGovernor.sol:478) and idempotence `AlreadyConsumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:479), then sets `consumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:480) one-way. Leader maintenance: consuming the leader promotes the carried runner-up when it is still live at `_runnerVotes` (CauldronGovernor.sol:489), else falls back to the bounded rescan `_recomputeLeader` (CauldronGovernor.sol:495); both slots are then cleared at `_runnerId` (CauldronGovernor.sol:497). Because this call sits inside relaunch, any revert downstream of it rolls the consumption back with the transaction (DERIVED).

nodes.name: getProposal
nodes.signature: function getProposal(uint256 id) external view returns (Proposal memory)
nodes.reachability: Unrestricted view. Copies the whole proposal, five strings included, into memory `_proposals` (CauldronGovernor.sol:513) and reverts `UnknownProposal` (CauldronGovernor.sol:514) for an id never written. No gate, no state change, no value.

nodes.name: _bestUnconsumed
nodes.signature: function _bestUnconsumed() private view returns (uint256)
nodes.reachability: Private; reached from `winner` (CauldronGovernor.sol:451) and `hasProposals` (CauldronGovernor.sol:470), hence from the registry's relaunch path. The fast path returns the cached `_leaderId` (CauldronGovernor.sol:526) only when it exists, is unconsumed, has votes and its window has closed at `votingEndsAt` (CauldronGovernor.sol:525); a proposal still taking votes therefore cannot be launched. Any miss pays the bounded scan `_recomputeLeader` (CauldronGovernor.sol:528), and returning zero is what makes relaunch revert.

nodes.name: _recomputeLeader
nodes.signature: function _recomputeLeader() private view returns (uint256 bestId, uint256 bestVotes)
observations: the doc block for `MAX_LEADER_SCAN` (CauldronGovernor.sol:550) still describes bounding a scan over the proposal list at 64; code no longer reads that constant here - the loop bound is `BENCH_SLOTS` (CauldronGovernor.sol:560) - so the constant is retained but unused by this function
nodes.reachability: The rescan behind `_recomputeLeader` (CauldronGovernor.sol:528), reached from `hasProposals` (CauldronGovernor.sol:470) and from `winner` (CauldronGovernor.sol:451) - i.e. on the relaunch path - whenever the cached leader is consumed, gone or still taking votes at `votingEndsAt` (CauldronGovernor.sol:525). It now iterates the fixed 8-slot bench at `_bench` (CauldronGovernor.sol:561) instead of a window over the most recent proposal ids, which is what removes the flood: ids were mintable by any single MiFren holder with no cooldown, so a voted, settled, unconsumed mandate could be pushed out of a positional window. Each candidate must still exist and be unconsumed at `consumed` (CauldronGovernor.sol:564) and must have CLOSED its voting window at `votingEndsAt` (CauldronGovernor.sol:565), and the comparison is strict at `bestVotes` (CauldronGovernor.sol:566) so ties keep the lower bench slot rather than the earlier proposal.

nodes.name: getPastVotes
nodes.signature: function getPastVotes(address account, uint256 blockNumber) external view returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the immutable mifrens address)
nodes.reachability: Declaration only: `getPastVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:5) has no body here. It is called once, in vote at `getPastVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:471), against the proposal's stored `snapshot` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:471), and a zero result reverts `NoVotingPower` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:472). The callee is the immutable set at `mifrens` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:373), so a deployment that wires a contract without this selector makes every vote revert (DERIVED).

nodes.name: getVotes
nodes.signature: function getVotes(address account) external view returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the immutable mifrens address)
nodes.reachability: Declaration only: `getVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:6) has no body here. It is called once, as the proposal-threshold gate `getVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:416), where a live balance below `PROPOSAL_THRESHOLD` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:416) reverts BelowProposalThreshold. Unlike the ballot weight it is read LIVE, not at a snapshot, so threshold power can be borrowed for the length of one transaction (DERIVED).

nodes.name: getPastTotalSupply
nodes.signature: function getPastTotalSupply(uint256 timepoint) external view returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the immutable mifrens address)
nodes.reachability: Declaration only: `getPastTotalSupply` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:15) has no body here. It is the quorum denominator, called once at `getPastTotalSupply` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:887) inside the pass test, measured at the proposal's `snapshot` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:887) and scaled by `QUORUM_BPS` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:887). Every path that decides an outcome runs through it: `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:563) in execute, `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:721) inside the bench scan's executability test, `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:721) and the public `passing` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:897), so a reverting or missing implementation blocks execution entirely.

nodes.name: allowedQuote
nodes.signature: function allowedQuote(address quote) external view returns (bool)
nodes.authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the immutable registry address)
nodes.reachability: Declaration only: `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:19) has no body here. It is called twice on the immutable `registry` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:374): once when a rotation target is named at `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:420) and again when the envelope is installed at `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:594), both reverting QuoteNotAllowed. The implementation is the registry's public mapping `allowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:321), writable only through the owner-gated `setAllowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:308) — so the allowlist is outside the reach of any vote here.

nodes.name: usdPerRawUnit
nodes.signature: function usdPerRawUnit(address quote) external view returns (uint256)
nodes.authority: anyone (declaration only, no body; dispatched on the guardian-set quoteOracle address)
nodes.reachability: Declaration only: `usdPerRawUnit` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:24) has no body here. It is called once, at `usdPerRawUnit` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:938), and only when the target is non-native and an oracle is wired; a zero price reverts `QuoteNotPriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:938). The address is the mutable `quoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:936), which the guardian may repoint at any contract via `setQuoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:943), so this call is to an address an admin controls (DERIVED).

nodes.name: conversionFor
nodes.signature: function conversionFor(uint16 spendBps, uint16 sliceBps) external pure returns (uint16)
nodes.reachability: Unrestricted pure helper with no storage access and no caller inside this file; it exists for user interfaces that must translate a spend budget into the share of the position it converts. Both arguments are caller-supplied, so the loop trip count `n` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:319) is spendBps divided by sliceBps and is bounded only by the uint16 range — up to 65535 iterations when `sliceBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:319) is 1, which is a caller-paid cost in a view call (DERIVED). Each step multiplies before dividing at `rem` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:323), truncating toward zero, so the remaining share rounds DOWN and the reported conversion at `rem` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:325) rounds UP (DERIVED).

nodes.signature: constructor( IVotes721 _mifrens, address _registry, address _guardian, uint64 votingPeriod, uint64 envelopeLifetime, uint64 cooldown, uint64 executionWindow, bool testnet )
nodes.reachability: Runs once at deployment and is the only writer of every timing parameter. Zero arguments fall back to the mainnet defaults at `MAINNET_VOTING` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:379) and its three siblings; unless `testnet` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:384) is passed, the one-day floors at `MIN_VOTING` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:385), `MIN_COOLDOWN` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:386) and `MIN_EXEC_WINDOW` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:387) apply, and in BOTH modes a lifetime shorter than the execution window reverts `BadTiming` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:392). No floor exists on `ENVELOPE_LIFETIME` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:395) itself beyond that coherence test, and neither `mifrens` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:373) nor `registry` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:374) nor `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:375) is checked for zero or for code, so a mis-wired deployment is only detectable later: a zero guardian dead-ends `cancel` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:616), `setGuardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:631) and `setQuoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:943) forever (DERIVED).

nodes.name: propose
nodes.signature: function propose(address quote, uint16 maxTotalBps) external returns (uint256 id)
nodes.reachability: Permissionless above a MiFrens threshold at `PROPOSAL_THRESHOLD` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:416); the size is bounded at `MAX_ENVELOPE_BPS` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:417), and the destination must be both allowlisted at `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:420) and oracle-priceable at `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:421), both re-checked at execution. Proposals COMPETE rather than queue - only the ENVELOPE is exclusive, refused while one is live at `ProposalActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:437) or inside `CooldownActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:438) - so a spammer cannot hold a single slot and veto treasury governance. The vote snapshot is now the PREVIOUS block at `snapshot` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:455): taking it at the current block let a proposer file and then acquire MiFrens later in the same block, because `getPastVotes` at an unsealed block counts transfers that land after the proposing transaction. Voting closes a fixed `VOTING_PERIOD` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:444) after filing.
nodes.authority: anyone holding at least PROPOSAL_THRESHOLD MiFrens of live voting power
nodes.value: none - filing a proposal moves nothing (DERIVED)

nodes.name: vote
nodes.signature: function vote(uint256 id, bool support) external
nodes.reachability: Permissionless once per address per proposal: unknown ids are refused at `UnknownProposal` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:467), a closed window at `VotingClosed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:468), a repeat at `AlreadyVoted` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:469), and zero checkpointed power at `NoVotingPower` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:472). Weight comes from the proposal's own snapshot at `getPastVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:471). The `_leadId` hint is maintained here, where the counts move: the incumbent growing at `_leadVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:487), the first-ever support at `_leadId` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:491), an overtake that dates the displaced rival at `_openVotedAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:498), the ONLY branch that lowers the bar - retiring a hint that is provably dead and older than a full vote-plus-execution window at `_dead` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:502) - and otherwise just re-dating at `_openVotedAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:525). NEW: a FOR-vote also enters the fixed 8-slot bench at `_benchRecord` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:528), which is what `winner` now falls back to instead of any scan over the proposal list. AGAINST-votes are counted at `againstVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:475) but touch neither the hint nor the bench (DERIVED).
nodes.authority: anyone holding checkpointed MiFrens power at the proposal's snapshot

nodes.name: _benchRecord
nodes.signature: function _benchRecord(uint256 id, uint256 votes) private
nodes.reachability: Reached only from a supporting vote at `_benchRecord` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:528). An id already tracked returns immediately at `b` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:539); otherwise the incoming FOR-total must beat the WEAKEST live entry at `weakVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:549). Entries that can never execute again are valued at zero through the monotone `_dead` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:545) - the same test the hint retires on - so dead slots are reclaimed before live ones. Fixed `BENCH_SLOTS` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:537) iterations, so the cost does not grow with the proposal count (DERIVED).
nodes.authority: private (single caller: vote, on a FOR-vote only)
observations: eight slots bounds how many mandates can be tracked at once at `BENCH_SLOTS` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:209); a ninth passing proposal weaker than every incumbent never enters, so `winner` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:667) cannot elect it once the `_leadId` fast path misses (DERIVED)

nodes.name: execute
nodes.signature: function execute(uint256 id) external
nodes.reachability: Permissionless. Order of refusals: unknown id at `UnknownProposal` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:560), vote still open at `VotingOpen` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:561), already executed or cancelled at `AlreadyExecuted` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:562), failed the majority-plus-quorum test at `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:563), not the chosen leader at `winner` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:568), and past its execution window at `EXECUTION_WINDOW` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:571). NEW: the two gates `propose` applies are now applied here too - no second envelope while one is live at `ProposalActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:590) and none inside the cooldown of the last at `CooldownActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:591). Without them, two proposals passing in the same window could both be executed: the first installs an envelope and stamps `lastEnvelopeAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:609), the loser then becomes the leader because the winner is executed, and executing it overwrote the live envelope with `movedBps` and `movedPrimaryBps` reset to zero at `envelope` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:601) - two full budgets inside one cooldown. A guardian cancel clears only `active` at `active` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:619) and not the stamp, so an emergency stop does not reopen the window. The allowlist and the oracle are re-checked last at `allowedQuote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:594) and `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:598).
nodes.authority: anyone (permissionless, by design - an approved rotation must not need a privileged executor)
nodes.value: no asset moves here - it installs the envelope that later authorises `rotateSliceFrom` to move liquidity, at `envelope` (line 601)
observations: comment at `propose` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:572) cites those two gates as ':387-388'; code has them at `ProposalActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:437) and `CooldownActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:438), so the in-comment line numbers have drifted

nodes.name: cancel
nodes.signature: function cancel(uint256 id) external
nodes.reachability: Only the address in `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:617) reaches this; everyone else reverts NotGuardian. It accepts ANY id, including one never proposed and one whose vote is still open, and writes `cancelled` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:618) unconditionally; a later proposal that draws that id overwrites the whole struct at `proposals` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:441), so a pre-marked slot does not persist (DERIVED). The live envelope is only stood down when the cancelled proposal is the one that installed it, via the `executed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:619) test, and `lastEnvelopeAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:609) is NOT rewound, so the cooldown from the cancelled envelope still runs against the next `propose` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:415) (DERIVED). The guardian can stop but cannot start or redirect a rotation: no path here writes `quote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:602) or `maxTotalBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:603).

nodes.name: setGuardian
nodes.signature: function setGuardian(address g) external
nodes.reachability: Guardian-only hand-off of the guardian seat. Zero is now REFUSED at `BadParam` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:633): the guardian is the sole caller of `cancel` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:616) and of the oracle setter, and this setter is itself guardian-gated at `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:632), so burning the seat would dead-end the emergency stop permanently with no way to appoint a replacement. There is no two-step acceptance, so a typo'd non-zero address still loses the seat irrecoverably (DERIVED).
observations: comment at `cancel` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:625) cites cancel at ':518'; code has it at `cancel` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:616) (DERIVED)

nodes.name: winner
nodes.signature: function winner() public view returns (uint256 best)
nodes.reachability: Public view that `execute` gates on at `winner` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:568), so it sits on the ONLY path that installs an envelope. Fast path: the `_leadId` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:671) hint is returned only after the same executability test the fallback applies, at `_executable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:672), so a stale or beaten hint costs a scan rather than electing the wrong proposal. The fallback is now the fixed 8-slot bench at `_bench` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:707) - not the original unbounded `1..proposalCount` loop, and not the positional newest-64 window that replaced it, because a window over a list anyone may grow is a window anyone may flood. Candidates must be executable at `_executable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:710) and the comparison is strict at `bestVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:711). Cost is O(1) in the proposal count (DERIVED).
observations: the doc block above still describes a time-bounded BACKWARDS walk over proposal ids stopping at the first too-old proposal, at `votingEndsAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:690); code walks only `_bench` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:707) and never touches `proposalCount`, so that description no longer matches the loop it precedes

with the bench fallback, ties break to the LOWEST BENCH SLOT rather than to the lower proposal id promised by the header at `Ties` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:642); bench slots are assigned by displacement order, so the tie-break is no longer id-deterministic (DERIVED)

nodes.name: _executable
nodes.signature: function _executable(Proposal storage p) private view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: Private; the single call site is the fast path in `_executable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:672). It is the one definition of executability: unknown, executed or cancelled proposals fail at `votingEndsAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:718), a still-open vote fails at `votingEndsAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:719), a stale one fails at `EXECUTION_WINDOW` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:720), and the remainder must clear `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:721). Because it is a superset of the scan's own tests, trusting the hint can only elect a proposal the scan would also accept, though not necessarily the highest-voted one unless the hint is maintained as a maximum (DERIVED).

nodes.name: _dead
nodes.signature: function _dead(Proposal storage p) private view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: Private; reached only from the hint-retirement branch at `_dead` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:502). It is monotone: `executed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:737) and `cancelled` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:737) are one-way flags and the deadline at `EXECUTION_WINDOW` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:738) only recedes, so a true answer can never become false. An id that was never proposed reads dead because `votingEndsAt` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:738) is zero (DERIVED).

nodes.name: allowance
nodes.signature: function allowance() public view returns (address quote, uint16 remainingBps)
nodes.reachability: Read by the rotation path at `allowance` (RedemptionExt.sol:303) and by `consume` itself at `allowance` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:830). Returns (0,0) for an absent or expired envelope at `active` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:755) and for a spent one at `spent` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:776), which is why the REMAINDER rather than the destination address is the liveness flag - address(0) is a legitimate destination. NEW: the counter it meters against depends on the size of the mandate at `BPS_ONE` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:775) - a full-position mandate reports progress from `movedPrimaryBps`, anything smaller from the shared `movedBps`. That closes a starvation shape: `movedBps` counts every slice including ones a stranger takes out of a secondary leg, so reporting the shared remainder let the voted migration budget be spent on side pools until the remainder hit zero while `movedPrimaryBps` was still zero, leaving the migration uncompletable and the 7-day cooldown blocking a replacement.

nodes.name: migrationMandateSpent
nodes.signature: function migrationMandateSpent() external view returns (bool)
nodes.authority: anyone (the registry rotation path is the production caller)
nodes.reachability: Unrestricted view with one production consumer: the rotation facet redenominates a generation on it at `migrationMandateSpent` (RedemptionExt.sol:526), and only when the slice came from the primary leg. It returns true only when the guild budgeted at least one whole position `BPS_ONE` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:813) AND that budget has been spent out of the generation's own position `movedPrimaryBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:813), so secondary-leg slices counted in `movedBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:857) can never declare a migration complete. Because slices take a share of CURRENT liquidity, a spent budget does not mean a drained position (DERIVED).

nodes.name: consume
nodes.signature: function consume(uint16 bps, bool fromPrimary) external
nodes.reachability: Registry-only, called after a slice has already succeeded at `consume` (RedemptionExt.sol:459), which also reports whether the slice came out of the generation's own position. Liveness is tested on the REMAINDER at `left` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:837) rather than on a zero destination address, so an envelope rotating back to native ether is no longer indistinguishable from no envelope. NEW: the two kinds of slice are bounded by different budgets - a primary slice against the remainder `allowance` reports at `left` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:853), a secondary slice against the SHARED total at `movedBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:854) - so leg-to-leg rebalancing is still capped by the vote but can no longer starve the migration. Both counters advance at `movedBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:857), and only a primary slice advances `movedPrimaryBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:858), which is the sole counter `migrationMandateSpent` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:811) reads. Deactivation follows the SAME counter `allowance` reports at `movedPrimaryBps` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:870), so a spent envelope stops blocking `propose` instead of holding the slot until expiry.
nodes.value: none - accounting only; the liquidity has already moved in the caller (DERIVED)
observations: the registry gate reverts `NotGuardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:828), which names the wrong role for a registry-only check (DERIVED)

comment at `propose` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:860) cites propose's envelope gate at ':322' and cancel at ':409'; code has them at `ProposalActive` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:437) and `cancel` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:616) (DERIVED)

nodes.name: _passed
nodes.signature: function _passed(Proposal storage p) private view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: Private, reached from `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:563) in execute, `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:721) inside the bench scan's executability test, `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:721) in the executability test and `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:898) in the public view. Two conditions: a strict majority at `forVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:877), so a tie fails, and a quorum of `QUORUM_BPS` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:887) — ten percent — of the supply measured at the proposal's own `snapshot` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:887), not live, so minting or burning after the vote opens cannot move the bar. The comparison at `forVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:888) is inclusive, and the division at `need` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:887) truncates, so the effective quorum rounds DOWN (DERIVED).
observations: comment `vote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:881) says quorum is read at the same timepoint the vote weighs ballots and points at line 384; code weighs ballots at `getPastVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:471) and reads the denominator at `getPastTotalSupply` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:887).

nodes.name: _settled
nodes.signature: function _settled(uint256 id) private view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: Private and unreferenced: no call site exists for `_settled` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:891) anywhere in the file, so it is unreachable from every external entry and contributes no runtime behaviour (DERIVED). Had it been used it would report a proposal as settled once `executed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:893) or `cancelled` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:893) is set or its window has closed — a WEAKER condition than `_executable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:717) and a different one from `_dead` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:736).

nodes.name: passing
nodes.signature: function passing(uint256 id) external view returns (bool)
nodes.reachability: Unrestricted view for interfaces: it answers whether `_passed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:898) holds right now, with no timing test at all, so it reports on an open vote and on a long-stale one alike. An id that was never proposed reads false because both tallies are zero and the majority test at `forVotes` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:877) fails first (DERIVED).

nodes.name: _requirePriceable
nodes.signature: function _requirePriceable(address quote) internal view
nodes.reachability: Internal, reached from `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:421) when a target is named and again from `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:598) when the envelope is installed. Two exemptions make it a no-op: a native destination returns at `quote` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:935) and an unset oracle returns at `o` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:937). Otherwise it calls out to the guardian-controlled `quoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:936) and treats a zero price as fatal `QuoteNotPriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:938); a reverting oracle propagates and blocks both proposing and executing, and a guardian able to repoint `setQuoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:943) therefore controls whether any non-native mandate can be installed (DERIVED).
observations: comment `setQuoteAllowed` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:905) names the registry's allowlist setter; code in the registry declares it as `setAllowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:308) and writes the mapping at `allowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:321).

nodes.name: setQuoteOracle
nodes.signature: function setQuoteOracle(address o) external
nodes.reachability: Only the current `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:944) may write `quoteOracle` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:945), with no zero-check and no code-check, and it may be rewritten any number of times. Because the stored address is called during both `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:421) and `_requirePriceable` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:598), the holder of this setter can make any non-native quote unproposable and unexecutable, or clear the slot to skip the check entirely at `o` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:937) (DERIVED).
observations: comment `Timelock` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:941) says the oracle is timelock-set, and comment `timelock` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:48) says only the timelock adds assets; code gates this setter on `guardian` (TreasuryGovernor.sol:944) and the allowlist on the registry owner at `setAllowedQuote` (CauldronRegistry.sol:308).
